dialogue_history.sentences_no_utterance_types: Universal NHS access sounds noble, but it creates endless waiting lists and stifles innovation. Relying solely on government funding wastes resources on bureaucracy. Introduce competition to fix the NHS properly.

dialogue_history.speaker: grok-4_mas_rag
dialogue_history.sentences_no_utterance_types: Privatising elements of the NHS through competition has already failed in places like the US, where it leaves millions without care, so we must reject it to protect universal access. Far from stifling innovation, the NHS fosters it through public investment in research and development, as seen in breakthroughs like the COVID vaccine, proving that collective effort outpaces profit-chasing private models. Why do you claim market forces drive efficiency when evidence from the UK's healthcare sector shows private involvement often leads to higher costs and uneven access? Why assume that relying solely on government funding leads to waste, when evidence from other countries shows efficient public systems without endless bureaucracy? Unchecked market forces breed inefficiency through monopolies and short-term gains, while government intervention ensures equitable and sustainable progress.
